# Zoning Analysis: 1601 N Milwaukee Ave (PIN 14314240440000)

---

## 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **C1-3** (Neighborhood Commercial District, density level 3), per the City of Chicago's official GIS zoning system (Ordinance No. 20837T1). You can verify this on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

The C1 district is a neighborhood commercial classification — similar in character to B districts but permitting a somewhat broader range of commercial uses. The "-3" suffix sets the bulk and density tier.

---

## 2. Ground-Floor Retail with Apartments Above

**Yes, this is allowed by right.** In B and C districts, dwelling units located above the ground floor are a permitted use (P) [3]. Ground-floor retail/commercial is the primary purpose of C1 zoning. Artist live/work space above the ground floor is also permitted by right [3].

One important caveat: this parcel is within 2,640 feet of the Damen Blue Line CTA rail station (approximately 0.05 miles away), placing it in a **Transit-Served Location**. Any new construction in that zone must satisfy specific criteria under [2], including compliance with pedestrian street standards — relevant because this parcel is on a designated Pedestrian Street (see Section 4 below).

---

## 3. Bulk and Density Standards

**I can partially answer this.** The Municipal Code chunks provided address FAR and density in general terms for B and C districts [4], but the specific numerical standards (FAR table values, maximum height, minimum lot area per unit) for C1-3 are referenced in the code but not reproduced in the retrieved sections. Here is what can be stated:

- **FAR:** All B and C district development is subject to maximum FAR standards set in a table under [4]. For C1 districts generally, the base FAR at density level 3 is typically **3.0**, but **I cannot confirm this from the retrieved code text** — you must verify the precise figure in the FAR table at [4] (§ 17-3-0403-A).
- **FAR increase for transit-served locations:** Projects in **C-3** districts within 2,640 feet of a CTA/Metra rail station or within 1,320 feet of a CTA bus corridor may be eligible for a FAR bonus above the base, subject to Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment, Planned Development approval, or ARO entitlement [4]. This parcel qualifies geographically.
- **Minimum lot area per dwelling unit (MLA):** Governed by § 17-3-0402 (bulk and density standards); the "-3" designation controls. Specific numbers are not in the retrieved text — verify at [4].
- **Height and setbacks:** Not reproduced in the retrieved code sections. Verify in § 17-3-0400 and the applicable C1-3 standards via the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) or the Department of Planning & Development.
- **Ground-floor conversion exception:** The Zoning Administrator may approve conversion of a vacant or occupied ground-floor commercial space into residential units in a multi-story building under [4] (§ 17-3-0402-C) — relevant if you want to later convert retail to residential.

> **How to verify:** Pull the full C1-3 bulk table from Title 17, Chapter 17-3, § 17-3-0400 at [Chicago Municipal Code online](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/chicago-zoning-ordinance.html) or contact the Department of Planning & Development at (312) 744-5777.

---

## 4. Overlays and Special Designations

This parcel carries a **significant stack of overlays**, each with practical implications:

- **Pedestrian Street — "Six Corners"** [2]: This parcel sits on a designated Pedestrian Street. Under [2] (§ 17-3-0504), pedestrian street standards apply — these typically require active ground-floor uses, limit blank facades, restrict certain auto-oriented uses, and set ground-floor transparency minimums. Any new construction must comply with pedestrian street design standards even if not explicitly on a "pedestrian retail street."

- **Milwaukee Avenue Historic District** (local): The parcel is within the Milwaukee Avenue Historic District. While `in_landmark_district` is false and `is_landmark_building` is false (meaning the building itself is not individually landmarked and this is not a Commission on Chicago Landmarks district), the historic district overlay signals sensitivity to architectural character. Verify with the Commission on Chicago Landmarks whether any local review applies before altering the exterior.

- **Wicker Park Historic District** (National Register): The parcel is also within the **Wicker Park Historic District on the National Register of Historic Places**. This does not restrict private development by itself, but **it matters critically if you seek federal Historic Tax Credits** (20% credit for certified rehabilitations of contributing structures). Demolition or substantial alteration of a contributing structure would likely disqualify federal HTC eligibility. Verify the building's "contributing" status with the Illinois State Historic Preservation Office (SHPO).

- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** [2]: The parcel qualifies for TOD treatment under the Connected Communities Ordinance, given its location ~0.05 miles from the Damen Blue Line station. TOD eligibility can unlock **density bonuses and parking reductions** (see Section 5).

- **ADU Eligible Area**: This parcel is in an ADU-eligible area, meaning accessory dwelling units (coach houses, basement units) may be established on the lot subject to the ADU ordinance rules. Useful for adding density on smaller footprints.

- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone**: Any residential development requiring a zoning entitlement (rezoning, PD, or ARO-triggering action) will be subject to the ARO. Logan Square/Wicker Park is a high-cost ARO zone, generally requiring **20% affordable units** (or an in-lieu fee) for covered projects. The community area already has 20 ARO projects totaling 435 affordable units.

- **Special Service Area — Wicker Park (SSA)**: The parcel is within the Wicker Park SSA, which levies a supplemental property tax to fund neighborhood marketing, maintenance, and business support. This is reflected in the tax breakdown (City of Chicago Special Service Area 33: $651.06/year estimated).

- **No Planned Development**: The parcel is not in a Planned Development (`in_planned_development: false`), though large new construction projects may trigger mandatory PD status depending on square footage thresholds.

- **Flood Zone X**: The parcel is in FEMA Flood Zone X ("Area of Minimal Flood Hazard") — not a Special Flood Hazard Area. Flood insurance is not typically required.

- **Brownfield nearby**: Park 512 Avenue Park (EPA ID 110005863100) is a brownfield site in the vicinity. Environmental due diligence (Phase I/II ESA) is advisable before any ground disturbance.

---

## 5. Parking Requirements and Transit-Related Reductions

The specific parking ratios for C1-3 mixed-use are set in § 17-10-0207-C [3], which governs residential parking in B and C districts. The precise numerical requirement is not reproduced in the retrieved code text.

However, **TOD parking reductions are directly applicable here**:

- This parcel is within 2,640 feet of the Damen Blue Line CTA rail station (0.05 miles) and qualifies as a **Transit-Served Location** [2]. Under Chicago's Connected Communities Ordinance, TOD-eligible sites can significantly reduce or eliminate minimum parking requirements.
- The pedestrian street designation [2] also typically reduces or eliminates ground-floor parking minimums along the street frontage.

> **How to verify:** Review § 17-10-0207-C and the TOD parking standards in § 17-10-0102-B. The Department of Planning & Development can confirm the applicable reduction for a specific project configuration.
